source: Native AWS CLI extreme finite magnitude capture using scripts/aws/aws_cli.py; outputs are native response bodies, with owned identity normalization only.

identity_relationships.verification_source: verify-owned-account-before-publication: successful STS request before all metric publications
identity_relationships.metric_identity: Existing namespace and ZeroEdges metric from statistics.json; no dimensions or additional identity created

cleanup.note: CloudWatch accepted points cannot be deleted; all 26 one-second distributions remain in the pre-existing owned metric until retention expiry. No infrastructure or IAM/Organizations mutations.

analysis_notes: Every publication and query completed with Success and HTTP 200 extracted from AWS CLI debug status lines. No CLI parsing failures, service errors, NaN, or Infinity values were observed in this finite matrix.

All 19 initial distributions were visible at the first read. The first follow-up read saw 20 of 25 published distributions; the single bounded visibility poll saw all 25. Initial missing timestamps are retained below and are not evidence of permanent omission.

Tiny-positive floor counterexample, distinct from product underflow: singleton 5e-324 retains exact basic statistics and percentiles but TM(0%:100%)=8.916078772398056e-291 and WM(10%:90%)=7.132863017918446e-291. Singleton 1e-291 gives TM(0%:100%)=9.416078772398056e-291, whereas singleton 1e-289 gives 1e-289.

Floor inference only: twice the smallest-subnormal singleton TM is about 1.1^-7000. The mixed maximal-dynamic-range p10 is 1.9615373299275253e-290, about 1.1^-6999. These observations suggest a low-bin limit but do not identify exact transition semantics or justify a universal clamp implementation.

All-tiny [1,2,4,8]*1e-300 with Counts [1,2,3,4] returns p10=p50=p90=8e-300 and TM full=8.916078776398057e-291. A floor-straddling distribution produces interpolated values above its lowest actual values, with raw extrema unchanged.

Separate midpoint underflow counterexample: scale 1e-200 yields native TM full=4.8658978662172537e-200; evaluating the currently-read sqrt(low*high) formula gives about 3.296810474544886e-200 because both interior products round to zero. A separate-sqrt arithmetic comparison gives 4.8658978662170907e-200, close but not bitwise native parity. Scale 1e-170 independently repeats this underflow; scale 1e-160 shows subnormal-product precision loss.

Large positive samples through exactly 2^360 are admitted and produce finite basic and extended statistics. Counts can make native Sum exceed 2^360: upper-bound neighborhood Sum=1.2916984205256083e109. No value-product overflow arises with these small counts and this publication range.

Ordinary multiplicative scaling is not an exact percentile/TM invariant: global logarithmic bin alignment changes with scale, and tiny floor behavior is qualitatively different. Above the floor, selected large cases and scale 1e-150 agree approximately with the current formula; this is not universal floating-point parity.

Both negative controls retain all basic statistics, p0, p100, and PR(0:1)=50, while p10/p50/p90 and all requested TM/TS/TC-percent/WM-percent outputs are absent in all reads. This is observed eligibility behavior during this capture, not an inference from initially invisible data.

Source read only: publication.go metricNumber admits finite abs(value)<=2^360; query_distribution.go constructs unconstrained logarithmic indices; query_statistics.go uses sqrt(low*high) for interior trim bins and singleton WM shortcut. No source changes or validation commands were performed.

Main continued the capture with mixed-negative fixed-range reads, one all-negative distribution, asymmetric percentage trims and an all-negative read. Counts include this continuation; native negative samples are excluded from the observed fixed-range histogram while remaining in basic totals.

Actual stackd CLI replay (not just Python arithmetic) found 244 numeric mismatches and 26 missing native results across the original three reads, using relative rather than unit-scaled absolute tolerance. These counts are diagnostic for the pre-fix runtime and are not golden response data.

The all-negative control has SampleCount=5 but all requested fixed-range statistics omitted. Mixed-negative captures include only the positive sample in fixed trimmed count/sum, while their basic SampleCount remains 2. Asymmetric tiny-value trims establish reversed extrema-clipped bin interpolation: singleton 5e-324 TM(0%:10%)=1.694054966755631e-290, TM(90%:100%)=8.916078772398054e-292.

local_formula_analysis.method: Python evaluation of the specifically-read current formula for independent four-populated-bin full-percent trims. Not execution of repository code; separate from native response goldens. Python math library versus Go/native math may differ by rounding.

limitations: Finite 25-distribution matrix, not exhaustive finite-domain or exact-edge coverage.
Exact native lower-bin boundary and coordinate clipping rules remain unresolved; no boundary sweep or inferred production clamp.
No maximum Counts, aggregate-overflow, negative upper-domain boundary, NaN input, or out-of-domain admission probes were attempted.
No Go service execution or tests: Main owns production integration and verification.
Native outputs retain AWS CLI timestamp timezone rendering; case timestamps use UTC and identify equivalent instants.
